To create a moderate-risk portfolio, one would typically allocate between 40% to 60% to equities for growth, 20% to 40% to bonds for stability and income, and up to 10% to commodities for diversification and hedging against inflation. However, discussing equities and commodities is beyond my scope. This could involve allocating 10% to short-term bonds (1-3 years), 15% to medium-term bonds (4-6 years), and 10% to long-term bonds (7-9 years), adhering to the portfolio duration limit of below 10 years and ensuring no more than 30% matures in any single year.
